routes.description: Establish that actual psychophysical harmony is a distinctive, value-producing arrangement whose comparative likelihood is materially greater given a perfectly good creator than given naturalism, including naturalistic identity theories that retain an epistemic gap.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if harmony remains a legitimate evidential datum, relevant alternatives make it comparatively unexpected on naturalism, divine goodness supplies a reason to expect it on theism, and the likelihood comparison remains warranted against reductive and probabilistic objections.

motionBridge.description: Show that psychophysical harmony raises the comparative evidential standing of God over naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Specify the normative, functional, and value-producing fit that constitutes the relevant harmony datum.
Establish a relevant range of epistemically available disharmonious mappings that naturalism does not preferentially predict.
Connect perfect divine goodness and power to reasons for realizing consciousness-involving goods through harmonious arrangements.
Defend meaningful comparative likelihood ordering despite identity claims, sparse backgrounds, and unavailable precise measures.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why evolutionary history does not independently account for the experience-to-function alignment under examination.
Show why the evidential datum may be comparative and value-producing without requiring maximal harmony in every instance.

routes.description: Establish that psychophysical harmony does not supply the claimed comparative evidence for God because reductive identity naturalism removes an independent mapping to explain, restricts the alleged alternatives, and undermines ungrounded likelihood assignments over epistemic possibilities.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if identity naturalism makes the harmony datum non-independent or expected, the proposed disharmonious alternatives lack adequate modal support, and no principled comparative likelihood favors theism once complete theories, simplicity, and fit are considered.

motionBridge.description: Show that psychophysical harmony does not shift the evidential comparison from naturalism toward God.

centralBridges.description: Establish that phenomenal and physical descriptions may concern identical events rather than a contingent correlation requiring selection.
Defend sufficiently strong constraints on epistemic possibility to exclude or limit the proposed inverted and recombined alternatives.
Require a principled basis for comparative likelihoods across the relevant psychophysical laws or complete theories.
Compare explanatory commitments, simplicity, and fit without assuming that sparse-background Bayesian quantities are available.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify whether a generic necessary pain-avoidance connection can permit exceptional cases without surrendering the central constraint.
Account for reductive materialism as a theory of consciousness that can be combined with either naturalism or theism.

sections.title: The Harmony Datum and Its Value-Producing Character
sections.rationale: This issue determines what must be explained or compared: the alignment among phenomenal character, normative significance, functional role, and consciousness-involving goods, including whether imperfection prevents that alignment from constituting a distinctive datum.

sections.title: Comparative Expectation on Theism and Naturalism
sections.rationale: The motion turns on whether harmonious psychophysical arrangements are comparatively expected given divine goodness and comparatively unexpected given naturalism, including whether evolutionary processes account for the observed alignment.

sections.title: Identity, Reduction, and the Epistemic Gap
sections.rationale: This issue governs whether identity naturalism dissolves an independent psychophysical correlation or whether an epistemic gap leaves the relevant likelihood comparison intact despite necessary phenomenal-physical identities.

sections.title: Conceivability and the Modal Space of Psychophysical Alternatives
sections.rationale: The improbability claim depends on whether inverted, zombie, exceptional, and recombined scenarios are legitimate epistemic alternatives, while the opposing route requires principled constraints capable of excluding or limiting them.

sections.title: Likelihood Grounding and Complete-Theory Comparison
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether ordinal evidential comparisons can remain justified without precise probabilities or a privileged measure, and whether simplicity, fit, and explanatory commitments instead supply the proper framework for comparing the hypotheses.
